About Event

​AI is moving faster than most security programs can keep up with — agentic tools, MCP servers, and AI-generated code are shipping into production every day, often outrunning the guardrails meant to protect them. This hackathon brings developers and security practitioners together to get hands-on with the skills defining the new discipline of AI Security Engineering. Working in teams, participants will tackle real-world AI security challenges spanning the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications, threat modeling AI/agentic systems, securing MCP servers and agent skills against tool poisoning and supply-chain attacks, hardening vibe-coded applications, and red-teaming a live chatbot to find and exploit vulnerabilities before attackers do.

​Whether you're a developer curious about securing AI-powered apps or a security specialist looking to apply your skills to LLMs and agents, you'll leave with practical, portfolio-ready experience — and the kind of muscle memory that only comes from breaking (and fixing) real systems. No prior AI security experience required — just a builder's mindset and curiosity about where AI meets attack surface.

Generative AI Short Film Hackathon
Generative AI Short Film Hackathon

A hands-on generative AI hackathon in SF this September, partnered with Machine Cinema, where ~20 teams build and premiere short AI films to push the future of iterative media forward.

Yasmeena Faycurry
Follow
Published Jun 15, 2026
Last modified Jun 15, 2026
00
Media is becoming iterative.
For a century, a film was a finished thing. Made once, shipped once, watched. That is ending. The new model is media that gets made, remixed, and reshaped continuously, by small teams using tools that turn an idea into a finished frame in an afternoon.
Film is one of the biggest mediums this reshapes, and we want to bring the people rebuilding it in one room.
This September we're hosting a generative AI short film hackathon in San Francisco, with Machine Cinema, the most active community of AI filmmakers working today.
The format is simple. About 20 teams of three or four. A few hours to make and premiere a one to three minute animated short, using the latest tooling across video, image, audio, and world models.
A medium doesn't move forward in essays about it. It moves forward when the people defining it are in the same room, making things.
Come build with us!
